name: DJ Snake
notes: A French producer bridging trap, moombahton and big-room, whose documented approach is "a fusion of European dance music and hip hop beats". The modelled band runs from the lowest tempo the entry states, "~108 for moombahton", up to the top of its big-room band, "126-130 for the big-room material". The third documented band, "140-150 for the trap material with a half-time feel", is a different rhythmic family and is named here rather than folded in, since the compendium's rule is that families are picked and never blended. ⚠ INFERRED: the entry states 108 as a point and 126-130 as a band, so the 109-125 interior of the modelled range is a continuity choice rather than a documented span; nothing below 108 appears in the entry. The drums encode the moombahton grammar the entry describes: "a slowed electro-house kick with a dembow accent replacing the plain backbeat", so the kick anchors on 1 with a 0.36 tresillo bias and the snare keeps its 2&4 placement while a high-probability ghost set carries the dembow figure; the trap side contributes the 32nd hat rolls and the sparse kick, and the big-room side the tuned kick with minimal percussion, which is why the perc bed stays at 2-5 hits a bar rather than the full Latin battery. `bass808` is `counter_riff` for the documented "808 sub with pitch glides in the trap mode" so the distorted house saw survives as the bassline. His harmony is "minor-mode two- or four-chord vamps with pentatonic melodic material", with the best-known crossover "built on a static modal loop with the melody doing all the work" `[LOW-CONF]`, a mark repeated here — hence a `vamp`-weighted harmonic rhythm and a riff-loop melody on the documented pitched flute/pan-pipe palette. His method is "fast and remote — a signature remix completed in roughly four hours with vocals emailed in", and the arrangement makes hard cuts between sections. ⚠ The research calls the tempo and drum grammar convention-derived; every velocity, density and probability above is INFERRED. ⚠ **`chords.harmonicRhythm` re-weighted (2026-08-17, harmony variety floor).** The entry's harmony line is "minor-mode two- or four-chord vamps with pentatonic melodic material", and the engine's `vamp` value is *one* chord held for the whole clip (`generators::chords`: "One chord for the whole pattern") — so weighting `vamp` at the top rendered a **one**-chord bed the research nowhere describes. The chord motion the entry states is now carried by `1_per_bar` (the pair over a 2-bar cell) and `2_bars_per_chord` (the pair over a 4-bar cell), with `vamp` kept as the minority for the held reading. A four-chord vamp needs four slots, which only `1_per_bar` gives; the entry's "static modal loop" reading is what `vamp` keeps. ⚠ The split between those two rates is **INFERRED** — the entry names the device, not its rate.
